note: Recast from the redescription of S. seclusus by Bourguignon & Roisin (2011), the original in English; the soldier (both large and small) is described, the alate is recorded as Unknown, and the original gives no mesonotum measurement. In the original the holotype value of hind tibia length in the large soldier, 1.76 mm, lies slightly outside its range of 1.43—1.73 mm, and the holotype value of head length to the labral tip in the small soldier, 1.52 mm, lies below its range of 1.59—1.97 mm; both are entered as printed and are probably typesetting or scanning errors.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text:
Large soldier: body large. Head with about 30 setae; labrum short and large, not reaching the mandibular tips; antenna usually 17 segments, occasionally 16 or 18; pronotum large, with about 15 setae, mainly on the margins; abdomen densely hairy, with 20—40 setae per segment; mandibles moderately curved; first marginal tooth of the left mandible shorter than the second, with a small boss at its base; right mandible with a slight basal boss. Measurements (mm, 1 individual from the type colony; in parentheses 30 large soldiers from 10 colonies): head length to the anterior margin of the postclypeus 2.07 (1.82—2.33); head length to the labral tip 2.52 (2.24—2.74); maximum head width 1.96 (1.69—2.05); pronotum width 1.27 (1.08—1.42); right mandible length 1.27 (1.00—1.36); minimum postmentum width 0.36 (0.22—0.38); hind tibia length 1.76 (1.43—1.73).

Small soldier: body large. Head with about 15 setae; labrum 1.5 times as long as wide, reaching the mandibular tips; antenna 16 segments; pronotum large, with about 10 setae on the margins; abdomen hairy, with 10—15 setae per segment; mandibles large, strongly curved. Measurements (mm, 1 individual from the type colony; in parentheses 10 small soldiers from 10 colonies): head length to the anterior margin of the postclypeus 1.11 (1.10—1.41); head length to the labral tip 1.52 (1.59—1.97); maximum head width 0.86 (0.95—1.19); pronotum length 0.44 (0.38—0.48); pronotum width 0.66 (0.68—0.86); right mandible length 0.75 (0.79—0.97); maximum postmentum width 0.35 (0.34—0.39); hind tibia length 1.09 (1.01—1.32).

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: It is readily distinguished from the other species of the genus by its large size and by the densely hairy abdomen in both the large and the small soldier; the small soldier varies greatly in size and may comprise two developmental subclasses (Miller 1987). The alate is not known. It is distributed in southern New Guinea and also occurs in Queensland, Australia.
